task.title: Address Unit C exact review findings

events.content: Treat dirty and deletePending as one pending-mutation state: Treat dirty and deletePending as one pending-mutation state

raw.question: Treat dirty and deletePending as one pending-mutation state
raw.chosen: Treat dirty and deletePending as one pending-mutation state
raw.reasoning: The Syncer persists both as authoritative work not yet accepted remotely. Every aggregate count and destructive preflight must share that definition or failed deletes disappear from status and safety checks.

events.content: Pass persisted scope roots into writeback-list reconstruction: Pass persisted scope roots into writeback-list reconstruction

raw.question: Pass persisted scope roots into writeback-list reconstruction
raw.chosen: Pass persisted scope roots into writeback-list reconstruction
raw.reasoning: Private state can be durable before the public child snapshot. The catalog scope is already known and remains authoritative when .relay/state.json is absent, so re-deriving it from an optional artifact creates false root paths.

retrospective.summary: Addressed all three Unit C review findings: disconnect checks private dirty/delete-pending state, aggregate counts include pending deletes, and writeback list uses persisted scope roots when public state is absent. Focused regressions pass.
